interest: This document offers insight into the social and cultural life of American expatriate communities in interwar Japan during early 1932, a period marked by escalating geopolitical friction following the Manchurian Incident and the Shanghai Crisis of January 1932. It illustrates the U.S. State Department's decimal filing and cross-referencing practices, connecting records of domestic cultural commemorations (decimal 811.415) to records on foreign entertainment and private societies in Japan (decimal 894.46211). For historians, it provides valuable evidence of how American national observances like the Washington Bicentennial served as focal points for expatriate community cohesion and public diplomacy amidst deteriorating Japanese-American relations.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State Document File cross-reference sheet dated March 1, 1932, concerning Despatch No. 424 from Tokyo prepared by Arthur Garrels. The sheet cross-references the primary record filed under 811.415 Washington Bi-Centenary/730 into the Japanese internal affairs decimal classification 894.46211 (Entertainment in Japan by Private Persons and Societies). The underlying report documents celebrations organized by the American resident communities of Tokyo and Yokohama to commemorate the bicentennial of George Washington's birth.
